main_body: A flat repeating green grass-like ground patch, labelled desert. It is a terrain texture with no standing volume.
top_band: none (flat terrain texture, no top/front structure)
evidence: Terrain ground tile with no standing object. The column scan shows only a repeating pattern of grass tone dots (L=85-170) across the whole height, with no top band and front face. The 3/4 contract does not apply to flat ground, so it is not penalised.

style.evidence: The candidate uses only 5 distinct colours, with a median of 5 per tile, against 80 distinct and 26 per tile for the grass reference. Texture is a regular repeating dot/cross motif of light and dark green on a single mid green base, so it reads as a mechanical tiled pattern, not hand-shaded clumps. It has no flat fills, and the 4 or so lightness steps are fewer than Beodeul's 5-6. The paving reference is also at 7 colours, but the grass reference is the same kind and far richer. The candidate is also green, not sandy, although hue is not judged. It is much lower in density than the grass reference and looks thinner next to it.
